# generator-shortcuts

The strongest plausible shortcut is **paint every cell in each cyan component's
bounding box**, using the same inset/quadrant colors as the intended rule. It
fits every canonical demonstration because all canonical cyan components are
solid rectangles, so object cells and bounding-box cells coincide.

An exact disagreement is stored at
`repo/generators/04ec2218e2d8/counterexamples/semantic-shortcuts/bbox_fill_minimal.json`.
It is generated by:

- seed `2180`
- sample index `37061`
- difficulty `easy`
- `scene_profile="two_generalized"`
- `component_style="edge_notch"`

The file contains the complete 23×23 input and both complete outputs. Its two
components have 6×6 bboxes, the minimum total bbox area (`72`) admitted by the
grammar. The intended rule leaves the input's two notches black at zero-based
coordinates `(10,17)` and `(12,8)`; the rival paints both cells blue (`1`).

I checked the input three ways. `self_check` accepts it; the selected canonical
Racket application in `checks/counterexamples/bbox_fill_racket.json` produces the
stored canonical output with executed rule hash `6d0c8228b329`; and the declared
Python rival produces the stored alternative output. The portable reproducer
`counterexamples/semantic-shortcuts/reproduce.py` binds the generator SHA-256
`705979abafe1f0f810601ed2e37f98b635b7a7c873b2fb8105790711847b52f5` and asserts
that those are the only two differing cells.

Yes. The proposed generator emits such cases by default: its period-3 schedule
cycles `solid`, `interior_hole`, and `edge_notch`, so two out of every three
ordinary sample indices carry direct evidence against whole-bbox painting.
The strict semantic sample observed 200 hole cases and 189 notch cases in 600
draws, and the source-bound lesson censuses found the rival refuted in every
materialized lesson and every required query rotation tested.
